An aquarium’s filter does far more than keep the water looking clean. It continuously removes waste, circulates oxygen, and provides a home for beneficial bacteria that break down harmful toxins produced by fish and uneaten food. Without proper filtration, ammonia and other toxic compounds can quickly build up, turning a healthy aquarium into a dangerous environment for its inhabitants. A good filtration system helps maintain water quality, stabilize the ecosystem, and keep fish healthy over the long term. While decorations and lighting may catch the eye, the filter is the unseen engine that keeps the entire aquarium alive.

The amount of times I hear “Your tank looks dirty, why don’t you clean it” is ridiculous (I am looking at you @Fish Shop Matt).  Water that is tinted a yellowy brown doesn’t always mean the tank is overdue a water change. Instead, many fishkeepers (like me!) do this on purpose to recreate the natural habitats of our fishes more closely.  The tinted water helps to create the dim and gloomy conditions of forest streams and swamps. Plus, the weakly acidic tannic and humic substances help to lower the pH, which is beneficial for many of the fishes we keep in aquariums. Next time you see a “tinted” aquarium I urge you to look a little closer, you may find beauty hidden in those gloomy waters. 🍂
Clear water isn’t just about aesthetics. It’s also a really good indicator of aquarium health.  #aquarium #aquascape #fishtank #plantedtank #fishtok
